description:
Auto Colonies
Automatic Faction and Colony management for Starsector 0.98a+0.98.5a.

Source code and guides
Required mods: None.
Updating: Delete the old mod folder in mods/ (Auto Colonies or Colony Manager), then extract the new one. Saves and settings carry over.
Safe to add mid-game

Breaks saves if removed

No known mod conflicts

Short summary
Colonies: Set your colony to Auto and have it place all your items, build all your buildings, and do everything a player would, automatically.
Costs: To keep it fair, every action it takes will cost a small amount of credits, which is changeable in options.

Long description
Intended setup: This is designed to work with as few as a single colony and as many as about 20, which is what I've tested it to. Basically, the idea is that you start playing the game, and you don't really have any difference in the early game. You'll be playing and playing and playing until you found your initial colony. Once you found said colony, you right-click on Population Infrastructure and click on Colony Autopilot, and then you can pick a mode.

Typically, I will pick Auto immediately and close it out, and then just let the colony manage itself. For the most part, it will make all the decisions in building all the buildings, deploying fleets, trying to defend itself, and managing itself. All I am responsible for is going around exploring, finding different planets, and trying to optimize where I want to have the empire relocated, but all the actual colony management itself is dictated to the mod instead of me.

Also, my job as the player is to go and explore and find colony items to give to the Autopilot, such as AI cores, nanoforges, synchrotron cores, and whatever else you can find. Put them in the Autopilot Storage, and then it grabs those and puts them where it thinks it should put them.
Modes: Currently working on a mod rewrite because the way it's implemented right now is poorly done. I would recommend currently just to use Auto if you're going to use this mod. The Advisor and Approve modes are basically identical currently. They just will show you in the Autopilot menu what it thinks the best buildings to build are, and have buttons for you to start the builds within that menu (with estimates for how much money they're going to earn and whether it's going to pay itself off in a good amount of time or not). I don't think that it's good now. I think once the rewrite's done, it'll be a bit better.

Features
Building
It automatically ranks the importance of buildings across all the mods that you have, or, if you don't have mods, just the vanilla buildings. It will try to build based on a balanced profile initially, or whatever profile you suggest, whether that's for ship hull construction, quality weapons, fuel, etc. It'll balance across them all, or it'll select income buildings primarily if that's what you would like. Items, AI cores and administrators
These are put depending on the doctrine you choose. There's storage for Autopilot specifically, and it will ship the items around, for a small fee and some time, to whatever colony needs the items, depending on how the buildout is running.
Money ladder and capital
The mod's been designed with a triage system for money, where it puts money where it thinks it's most important.
Initially, it'll stockpile until it hits a certain amount, and then it'll begin to grow colonies.
Once they've grown enough, it'll start to work on the military, then building new ships and more patrols.
It'll start to make new colonies.
It'll start to balance your entire economy.
It'll start building wonders and optimizing everything, as well as picking your biggest and usually first colony as your home port/trade hub/capital. That is also changeable in the settings.

War (Nexerelin)
There are several war levels, and we start with the Retaliate setting being the default, as well as a default stance for every faction that's in the game. If there is a mod that's not included, let me know, and I'll get it included.

Typically, the way this works is that if a war starts, we will retaliate until the war ends automatically. Your fleets will be made automatically, raid automatically, invade automatically, retake your planets automatically, etc. There are also options to attack Hegemony, AI inspections, Persean enforcement fleets, etc., for a cost  (off by default).
Security
Tries to protect colonies from outside threats and will typically be kicked on automatically if some invasion force arrives in the system. Or it can be manually set permanently to have a planet be a security-based planet. This is different from fleet production. This is mainly to protect the planet, not to project outward force. Optional Low profile style. New colonies (optional)
If this is enabled, it will use the Nexerelin colony fleet option to send colony fleets out to what it believes would be the most useful planet to your current set of worlds, basically to enhance your empire. Whatever is the closest and the most "optimal."

This can make mistakes and is only recommended once you have a relatively large empire and you're playing with limits off. Otherwise, I typically would not recommend using the automatic new colonies feature.

This would be something I would use if I had five colonies that were already size 5 population and I was playing with a 30-colony limit or something of that nature.
Costs
The balance of this mod is that everything it does, every action it takes, will cost you a bit of money. This is in order to try and balance the fact that it's all automatic. I will say that just the fact that all of this is automatic and fast is very busted compared to the base game.

Having what is essentially an omega-level AI just choose to automatically build out all of your colonies quickly and efficiently will usually result in you raking in credits and resources very quickly. I'm working on a version that you will have to slowly unlock capability for, but that's going to take some time. In the meantime, this is a very fast and easy way to get colonies under quick management. Audit page. Settings
Currently, there's a button in the Intel tab for the Colony Autopilot, as well as a button on the colony screen itself. Working on putting this in the F3 menu under LunaLib. Every setting

Getting started
Open a colony and click Colony Autopilot.
Pick a goal, or leave it on Balanced.
Set the mode to Auto and save the recommended setup.
Put items and AI cores into Autopilot Storage.

Auto starts building at once. Back up your save before trying it.
Guides: all guides

Status
Saves: Back up your save before updating.

Supported mods
All optional. Each integration turns on when its mod is enabled.
Large integrations
Nexerelin War level, faction stances, agents, diplomacy, sieges, colony fleets.
Ashes of the Domain (Vaults of Knowledge, Theory of Toolbox), Building Menu Overhaul Research, synergies, management styles, trade contracts, megastructures, wonders.
Terraforming Made Easy Special-world plans, terraforming, Domain-era stable location upgrades.
Industrial Evolution Ambassadors, edicts, VPC chips, specialized mining and refining, courier shipping.
Buildings and colonies
Terraforming & Station Construction (Boggled) Terraforming projects. Mining and siphon stations as new colonies (optional).
Random Assortment of Things Frontiers settlement.
Grand.Colonies Builds past 12 buildings, with the extra upkeep counted.
Substance.Abuse Breweries and recipes.
Volkov Industrial Conglomerate Viral contamination treatment first. Soil nanites only on vanilla farmland.
Roider Union Dives and Union HQ valued for the colony's own deposits. Roider Charters placed.
Planetary Shield: Access Control The shield valued as defense. Port kept closed while there are Pather cells.
Unknown Skies, What We Left Behind, Astral Ascension Their mining conditions and water worlds. Planetless colonies kept safe.
Niko's Scavengable Industries Builds known blueprints. Risky blueprints are left to you.
Junk Yard Dogs, Carter's Freetraders Resource forges and the Biolab, with illegal goods counted.
Vulpoids Organ Farms, Biotech Facility, colony items, Profecto administrators.
Yunru Industries, Yunru's Worlds, Slightly Better Tech-Mining (one thread for all three) Secondary Drydocks, Auxiliary Shipbays, richer Tech-Mining.
Rogue Planets Its 31 conditions and synergy pairs in build values. Story worlds left to you.
Kadur Remnant, JaydeePiracy, Corrupt.Officials, Tahlan Shipworks, Gladiator Society, SCY, CJY's Toy Box, AI-Retrofits, Blue, Oculian Armada Their conditions and income rules in build values. Their shipyards count toward production. Story planets and risky buildings left to you.
Auto Outfitting Plans producers for the goods its large weapon orders need.
Stations
Station Augments Augment loadout per station.
Interstellar Imperium, Knights of Ludd Their stations count like vanilla ones.
Items and AI cores
Emergent Threats (IX Revival) Antimatter Stabilizer conversion. Panopticon cores into the Surveillance Center.
Omega Core Everywhere, Astral Ascension Renewed Omega core placement.
United Aurora Federation Its colony items placed by what they do.
Oddisz's mods
Cloning Cloning industries built when faster growth pays off.
Reverse Engineered Private Arsenal Left to you.
Sol Renewed Builds in Sol priced for the crisis meter.
Toolbox Economy Curves, Coalesced Little Mods (forum thread, GitHub) Supported.
Other mods
Any other mod Deposits and items read from the game's tables. Buildings measured on a test colony.

Mod support requests go here or in GitHub issues.

Compatibility and permissions
Compatibility and known issues
Optional integrations: See Supported mods.
Tested with: A list of about 100 mods. Every release is checked offline against every combination of the supported mods.
Known conflicts: None known.
Known issues: Expect bugs. Report them here or as GitHub issues, with starsector-core/starsector.log, saves/common/colony_autopilot_diagnostics.json.data and your modlist. Permissions
Code: Free to use, change and reupload, in modpacks too. No credit needed. Do not sell it.
Assets: None. The mod has no art.

FAQ
Adding to a game in progress
Safe. Colonies start on Advisor. Removing the mod later breaks the save.

Colony crises
Low profile lowers the odds (first colony dialog, or Settings, Expansion style). Pirate and Persean League crises come from colony size alone.

Nothing is being built
Check the mode (Advisor only gives recommendations) and the budget.

AI use disclaimer
Some or all assets and code in this mod were created using AI tools:
Code, docs and offline build checks: Claude Opus 5.5 (through Claude Code).
Design and in-game testing: Mjolniar.
Training data: None added. Art: None.
